session: This round was opened by the SESSION as M0-a-06's HARDENING ROUND S10 (J237 (2): the M0 hardening phase's fix rounds, batched per owning item; J238: M0 is the bedrock — the default for an M0 row is FIX with an exact precaution and a pin; J567: the bar is an independent closing check's PASS on the evidence), on the rows J757 routes to this item, beside the re-triage's note for it (docs/validation/hardening-retriage-2026-11-09/plan.json, 'inFlightNotPlanned': 'S10 later: Q78, Q95, Q76 tx side'): RQ2's strip of a removed chain's `shape` rows (Q79), the kernel pin and `shape` rows, Q76 under R10, Q78, Q95, and the leg's declared shift. Each 'failing line' below is one such row — an open queue row routed to this item (docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md) or a row the item's latest closing check wrote into its notes file; its evidence names the SOURCE you MUST read whole before fixing; the fix shape and the pin are the re-triage's reading, binding unless the source or the code shows it wrong — then say so in your notes and do what the finding needs. THE RULES OF A HARDENING ROUND: (1) inside the item's owns and nowhere else — a row that needs another item's file is REPORTED, not built; FOR THIS ROUND the seats write inside THE WRITE SCOPE: M0-a-06's owns (plat/packages/kernel/src/tx/ and plat/packages/kernel/test/tx/, unchanged in M0-work.json) plus THE CROSS-ITEM SCOPE (LEG 2's OWN TEXT below); wherever this brief or plat/docs/build/M0.md §3 says 'inside the item's owns', read 'inside the write scope'; a change any other file would need, or any other change in a scope file, is REPORTED, not built; (2) every row gets a PIN (a test that is red without the fix; your mutant table shows each pin killing its mutant) unless the row is comment-only or asks for a choices row — then the text is the deliverable; (3) BEHAVIOUR: a hardening fix may move output where a defect is fixed — a DECLARED shift, stated in your choices row with the before and after (digests and goldens re-recorded in the same round, named), never silent; where a row offers alternatives, take the one the design's text supports and say which; a change of an operation's or stage's CONTRACT (its design-level behaviour, a record or file format, an exported API) is NOT yours — report it as a note for the session's ruling and leave the row at REPORTED; (4) J264 / N-58: the refusal census of the item's registered families before and after the round, never rising (a row whose fix makes a lawful input succeed lowers it and says so); (5) API frozen (J263 Q1): no export of a folder index or the barrel added, removed or renamed unless a row explicitly asks for one — then the index change is the row's and stated; message texts pinned verbatim where a row changes one (J263 Q6); (6) the gates, NEAR and RELATED@1000 as the brief above says, at W=1; (7) the item's notes file gains a section 'Hardening round S10' with the row-by-row outcome (fixed / pinned / reported, each with its evidence and mutant), and the round's choices row names every row it closes. The CLOSING CHECKER confirms every row's outcome with its own evidence (re-reading the source note or queue row), re-kills every pin's mutant, re-measures the refusal census, and judges new findings by the blocker rule only; a row left REPORTED with a stated contract reason is not a failing line. THIS IS LEG 2 OF A MERGED ROUND (the MERGED-ROUND RULE, J443): M0-a-02 S4 → M0-a-06 S10 → M0-a-05 S15, in that order, on ONE tree and ONE branch, no reset between, each leg with its own build, closing check, LANDED line and record; a leg launches only when the leg before it returned ok with check.verdict pass (each builds on the one before). RULINGS BINDING (each read by its own grep, never the 1.3 MB file whole: grep '^| J757 ' and grep '^| J776 ' docs/PROGRESS.md): J757 — RL4: the kernel-internal vertex role `shape` enters M0 as ONE step (the registry row with the version raised; the maintenance of the rows in tx; the write at the chain's commit, its register kind and the oracles); R10: the stale stamp after compactSlots / load is closed by the restore GENERATION, built and pinned in leg 2. J776 — the session's FINAL rulings R1 – R17 after the adversarial review (docs/validation/rq2-spec-2026-11-11/rulings-final.md, read WHOLE): they REPLACE the provisional rulings and overrule the spec draft wherever they differ; every line below is written under them, and where a line and the rulings file disagree, the rulings file binds and the seat says so in its notes. J777 — the fold's amendments to those rulings, binding with them (rulings-final.md, 'Amended at the fold'): M1 reads FEWER THAN TWO; the commit hook reads the log's `moved` beside `unflagged`; the maintenance runs after rule 3 (b)'s flag step and before step (c); the converse oracle reads AT LEAST TWO; the design text is AMENDMENT ab (docs/AMENDMENTS-2026-11-11ab.md, items 997 – 1005), binding on this round as written there. THIS SPEC TOOK ITS ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (J631 (2) (a); the round changes a persisted format): docs/validation/rq2-spec-2026-11-11/review/review.md — findings F1 – F20, the numbered changes and its 'Follow-up'; its probe scripts and logs beside it are evidence a seat may re-run in a mirror (they plant a `junction` row as a PROXY for `shape`). Also binding: J358 / N-61 (2) and plat/docs/build/checks/rulings-hardening-1.md §2 (RQ2) — its design sentence; its code consequence naming applyLanding / ownShapeVertex is set aside by R1; J238 (1)–(3), J264, J290 / N-58. ONE DEFINITION throughout (J776): e is an entity; 'an other row' on an edge is an edge row whose entity is not e (a river's shore and bank are ONE entity). THE GATE: the round opens on the head of M0-a-05 S14's LANDING (hash filled at launch) or later, when few rounds are in flight, and once the measured list is final (R15). M0-a-05 S14 changes insert/insertChain.ts (pass 5 after `passes`), insert/stretch.ts (Q77's exact helper), cutBack / tryCuts, caps.ts, router.test.ts's ratchet, register/s14-rescues.json and bfuzz.test.ts's N-7 GOLDEN — every cite below was read on the design head 6f98b464: re-read every one on the RESUME head; the files, functions and forms named are binding, the numbers are not. THE MEASURED LIST (J757 (3); J776 R15): MEASURED by the session 2026-11-11 / 12 (J779; evidence docs/validation/rq2-spec-2026-11-11/measured/units.txt and red-units.txt, the two scripts beside them): the whole suite, 83 test folders one per run, on a47e28ce with arena/roles.json at version 2 and the `shape` row appended, PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=25; then every red folder again on the UNCHANGED tree at the same strength. 74 folders green with the raise; NINE red, of which ONE is the raise's. NOTHING ELSE moves with the raise: no other item's test, so NO SEAM is owed for it and leg 1 turns the three green itself. THE HEAD (red on the unchanged tree for their own reasons): packages/kernel/test/arr — Q152's six bands tests (closing.test.ts ×2, dryrun.test.ts, hardening-s15.test.ts, restage.test.ts ×2); bench/test/site — 5 (summary.test.ts's canary, declared at J772; compose.test.ts 'relief-60 default seed 2 (test size) refuses at S5 …' and spike.test.ts ×3 on relief-60 seed 2 — M0-e-06's, with its round S4 in flight and the session's seam of J766); bench/test/calibrate 3, bench/test/host 2, bench/test/timing 8 — the reference-machine tests (J176: a cloud container is not the machine their pins name). A test on the list labelled THE RAISE is a DECLARED RED from leg 1's landing until the landing commit: never a failing line of any leg; a leg re-records only its own item's tests on it; the session's seams re-pin the rest in the landing commit. Reds labelled THE STRENGTH or THE HEAD are not the round's. WHAT GOES TO THE QUEUE AND IS NOT THIS ROUND'S (docs/validation/rq2-spec-2026-11-11/rulings-final.md, 'What goes to the queue'): (i) F8 — a STRETCH of a chain that ENDS at a two-key own point, or a rekey CUT there, clears that point's split flag (§2.2 rule 3 (b) compares whole row sets), so once the chain's rest goes the point stays on the other chain for ever — a queue row for a RULING on rule 3 (b)'s comparison; the round's design sentence and pins are scoped to a chain removed WHOLE and to a stretch's INTERIOR, and no pin asserts the other chain's restoration after a stretch end or a cut; (ii) the reverse order (C inserted first, A along it later, then C removed: the point stays on A) — N-13's canonical-form class, named in the design sentence's scope; (iii) three coincident chains with the base removed first (rows and flag stay) — a notes row; (iv) R17 (a): decode refusing a row whose role's `since` exceeds its chunk's version — M0-a-15; R17 (b): whether a cache written under an older registry version may be used at all — M1's loader; (v) R12: the wrong cause ('a savepoint was put back …') the two stale-slot messages name for a copy; (vi) R6: splitThrough's `row` refusing `shape` — M0-a-04; (vii) a kernel-side invariant for the converse oracle (R10) — M0-a-14's validator; (viii) R8: whether a `shape` row makes a vertex editable (`VertexSig`) — a notes row for M2a. A seat that meets one of these REPORTS it under its queue name and builds nothing for it. DECLARED REDS OF THE HEAD, never a failing line: Q152's six M0-a-09 bands tests (if M0-a-09's re-pin round has not landed), J176's Mac-reference bench tests, Q153's flake (testkit/test/determinism/dilation.test.ts; re-run alone). No timing bar is judged on these machines. THE SEATS: the session's tiers for a kernel item (J390 / J631 / J714), named at launch. THE WAITING RULE and the waiter as the brief above says. LEG 2's OWN TEXT. THE CROSS-ITEM SCOPE (J757 R10; J776 R13; M0-a-15 lends): plat/packages/kernel/src/io/compact.ts — in compactSlots, ONE statement on the new arena right after its createPlat, and its import; plat/packages/kernel/src/io/decode.ts — in rebuild (the body decodeArena returns), ONE statement on the new arena right after its createPlat, and its import; nothing else in either file. A fourth leg for M0-a-15 was weighed and not taken (R13). The scope's mechanics are M0-a-06 S9's entry's (the base mirror; THE SCOPE DIFF per scope file with its SHA-256s; the record claims tx/ and test/tx/ only; the CLOSING CHECKER confirms the scope by landed:verify's expected mismatch for M0-a-15 alone and by reverse-applying the diff); at the landing the SESSION re-lands M0-a-15's record on session/a06s10-scope-1 through tools/session/land_child.py. THE `shape` ROWS this leg's pins need are PLANTED — inside a COMMITTED batch (a tx callback calling the arena's addRole), at the chain's level and with the chain's entity, on a vertex the fixture's insertions made (review F12: a bare addRole between batches moves no version, writes no record and reaches no maintained digest; a raw removeRoleRow in a callback did not persist in the review's probe), and STRIPPED ONLY THROUGH THE WRITERS; leg 3 writes them. No src path of this leg WRITES a `shape` row; LINE 1's maintenance strips them and clears flags. THE CONTRACT READINGS this leg builds by ruling, not reported: J776 R3 (the maintenance M1 – M4), R4 (the pin rule), R6 (removeEdges' VertexRef refuses `shape`), R12 (the generation of a copy). THE DECLARED SHIFT: Q95's commit records (LINE 5) and nothing else — the maintenance and the pin rule move nothing on an arena without a `shape` row (no src path writes one until leg 3); the roots, the census and every committed outcome identical; S7's golden probe moves only on the batches LINE 5 names. THE ORDER OF WORK: LINE 3 (the generation: it touches the scope files; its pins first), LINE 1, LINE 2, LINE 6, LINE 5, LINE 4, then LINE 7 on the final sources. S9's frames stand: the undo log, mark / undoTo and S7's image pins (savepoint.test.ts) are not re-opened; a restore inside a batch stays refused. RED ON THE BASE versus REGRESSION: every pin below says which it is; 'the base' is leg 1's landed tree (the `shape` role registered, no maintenance). THE LIST FOR THE SESSION'S SEAMS: the design sentences, which are amendment ab's (docs/AMENDMENTS-2026-11-11ab.md, items 997 – 1005: binding as written there; the base is edited at the amendments' next apply pass); R12's stale docs — the `Stamp` doc in arena/resolve.ts (M0-a-02), the header of facade/stamp.ts (M0-a-16), decodeArena's doc ('version is 0'; M0-a-15); any other item's test that pins a generation value or a commit record's `faces` lists and moves (owner, file, test, before, after). Notes section 'Hardening round S10'; verdict plat/docs/build/checks/M0-a-06-s10.md; lanes build/M0-a-06-fix-s10 / check/M0-a-06-close-s10 (free at this writing; re-keyed by the session if a key appears); ledger ids the next free at build time.

lines.line: LINE 1 — THE MAINTENANCE OF `shape` ROWS (J776 R3; Q79; Q74; N-61 (2); review F1, F2, F8, follow-up 1–3): no tx path keeps, strips or settles a `(shape, e)` row, so wherever its chain stops passing through the vertex once — the chain removed whole, a stretch through or ending at it, a rekey's cut, one role of a two-row entity — the row stays an orphan that holds the vertex for ever, and where the OTHER chain goes (A removed while C lives) the vertex keeps a flag and a row that C inserted alone would never carry.

lines.required_change: BUILD ONE RULE (J776 R3), in tx (M0-a-06's own files), for every (shape, e) row on a vertex v: (M1) e's edge rows are on FEWER THAN TWO of v's incident edges → the row is stripped (e ends here or is gone; on THREE OR MORE — a later chain of the same entity under an 'any' role such as shore, bank, margin or border adds an edge at v, and no maintenance runs at an insert — the row is KEPT by M4: J777); (M2) else v does not carry VERTEX_SPLIT after the batch's flag steps → the row is stripped; (M3) else v has exactly two incident edges and NO other row (an edge row whose entity is not e) on either → the row is stripped AND VERTEX_SPLIT is cleared (logged in `unflagged`): v is e's own shape vertex and the arena equals e inserted alone; (M4) else the row is kept (the other chain still on a side, a rider, a crossing chain at v). WHERE IT RUNS: (i) in rewriteRows, on every call, for every vertex of the call's vstar carrying a `shape` row, AFTER rule 3 (b)'s flag step and BEFORE (c)'s vertex step and the dissolution (so (c) frees a vertex the strip leaves with no edge and no row, and the dissolution sees the settled rows and flag) — the rows it strips go through the arena door like every other strip, their keys noted; (ii) at the COMMIT of ANY batch (tx.ts, after `t.op = 'commit'` and before sweepVertexRows), for every live vertex in the log's `unflagged` carrying a `shape` row, and for every vertex in the log's `moved` that carries a `shape` row and no VERTEX_SPLIT (warp's commitStep clears a moved free vertex's flag and logs it in `moved` only — the rule's 'every vertex whose split flag the batch cleared'). ORDER: the rule decides each vertex once per call from the state after the flag step; no writer keeps its own strip of `shape` rows (the draft's per-path strip, its StretchRef end rule and the provisional rulings 8 and B are REPLACED); clearFinerIn's and rekey's existing row handling stands (both already strip or move the rows of their keys). PINS (kernel/test/tx/; the fixture A `invisible` L2 (3142, 2862)–(499, 2966); C `invisible` L2 (3142, 2862) (1800, 2915) (499, 2966), whose interior point lands exactly at (1800, 2915), splits A's edge 0.19 cm off its line and keeps VERTEX_SPLIT by C-0302 (3) (review p1-straight.log: CONFIRMED on today's code; v of degree 2, {A, C} on both sides); (shape, base:C) planted at L2 on v inside a committed batch; every arena compared by contentPrint, encoded chunk refs and level digests, every step asserting allProblems empty and readable(p)): (a) C removed whole → equal to A alone, v gone — RED ON THE BASE; (b) A removed while C lives → equal to C inserted alone at C's placed points (v unflagged, no row: M3) — RED ON THE BASE (review p1: the arena differs by exactly the flag and the row); (c) a chain D crossing at v (degree 4), A removed, then EITHER D removed → equal to C alone, OR C removed → equal to D alone — RED ON THE BASE; (d) a StretchRef removal of C's stretch THROUGH v → the row stripped, v dissolved with the stretch's other interior vertices — RED ON THE BASE; (e) a StretchRef removal of C's stretch ENDING at v → the row stripped (M1: e on one edge) — RED ON THE BASE (review F1); its flag is left as rule 3 (b) leaves it and no assertion about A's later restoration is made (F8: the queue's); (f) a rekey of C with its CUT at v → (shape, base:C) stripped at the cut (review p6) — RED ON THE BASE (the flag: F8, the queue's); (g) an entity e carrying two edge roles along the run, one role removed by removeEdges(ChainRef) → the row KEPT (e's other role still on exactly two edges) — a REGRESSION PIN (green on the base; kills ENTITY-STRIP, the draft's strip by entity on a chain's removal); (h) a rider R (a finer chain along A from one end to v, leaving there; the planted (shape, C) row at C's OWN level — at another level today's E_INVARIANT refusal fires, F12's level rule) removed → R's removal commits and v survives with flag and row (M4) — a REGRESSION PIN (review follow-up (b′): without the row today's code refuses R's removal E_INVARIANT); (i) a third chain x (0, 3501) (735, 705) (2456, 2886) attached at v and removed → v survives, print and digests equal to before x — a REGRESSION PIN (relevel's any-row guard); (j) clearFiner over an L2 C along an L1 A → the L2 row stripped and A's route restored — a REGRESSION PIN (clearFinerIn already strips the level's rows; CF-KEEP alone is EQUIVALENT under M1 and is stated so, killed only together with MAINT-OFF); (k) a rekey of C's stretch whose INTERIOR holds v → (shape, base:C) moved to (shape, to) and kept — a REGRESSION PIN (rekey moves interior vertex rows; RK-SKIP alone equivalent under M1, stated); (l) a batch that clears v's flag with no removal at v (a warp moving v's neighbour on its run, (b′)) → at commit the row is stripped (M2) — RED ON THE BASE. MUTANTS: MAINT-OFF (no maintenance) red on (a)–(f) and (l); FLAG-KEEP (M3 strips the row but keeps the flag) red on (b) and (c)'s D-removed branch; M3-ANYDEG (the flag cleared at any degree) red on (c)'s C-removed branch (v stays on D for ever); M4-STRIP (the row stripped at degree > 2 when no other row remains on e's edges) red on (c)'s D-removed branch (D's removal dissolves C's own point); HOOK-OFF (no commit-time pass) red on (l); ENTITY-STRIP red on (g). ONE MORE PIN (J777; M1's 'fewer than two'): (m) where the registry's role consistency lets it commit, a second chain of C's entity under an 'any' role inserted so that it adds a THIRD edge of the entity at v, then an unrelated removal that touches v → the row KEPT; then that second chain removed → v still carries its flag and its row — a REGRESSION PIN; mutant M1-EXACT (the row stripped unless the entity is on exactly two edges) red on it. If no such chain can commit at v (the builder says by which check), the notes say so and M1-EXACT is stated unreachable.
